history.period: 1915 onwards; Samadhi construction 1902/1904 onwards, still ongoing
history.summary: NON-HINDU: Dayalbagh is the headquarters of the Radha Soami (Sant Mat) faith, a non-denominational spiritual tradition founded in Agra on Basant Panchami 1861 by Param Purush Puran Dhani Soami Ji Maharaj (Swami Shiv Dayal Singh Ji); it is NOT a Hindu temple and needs a keep-or-drop decision for the temples dataset. The 'Dayalbagh Temple' is the faith's great white-marble Samadhi (mausoleum) in the Soami Bagh/Dayalbagh colony — a memorial to the founder whose construction began in the early 1900s, ran over a century (reports say 104-119+ years), and was declared open in 2018; the 193-ft structure in Makrana marble on a foundation of 52 wells is often compared to the Taj Mahal. The permanent satsang headquarters 'Dayalbagh' ('Garden of the Merciful') was established on Basant Panchami 1915 by the fifth Sant Satguru; it is a self-sustained colony with the Dayalbagh Educational Institute. Coordinates are for the Radha Soami Samadhi on Dayal Bagh Road (full-address geocode).

name: Dayalbagh Temple
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Dayalbagh is a green, self-sustained township about 8-12 km from central Agra on the Yamuna bank, known as the 'Lungs of Agra', and is the worldwide headquarters of the Radhasoami Satsang Dayalbagh faith.
tradition: Radha Soami / Sant Mat (non-denominational; NOT Hindu)
